content:
Below is the technical skills block of a resume. Every entry should be a real, named tool: a programming language, framework, library, cloud platform or cloud service, database, application, protocol or methodology - something a person installs, imports, signs in to or writes code in.

Some entries are not. They are CONCEPTS that slipped into the list: an activity, practice, ability, process, category, description or verb - "model performance measurement", "regression detection", "Model Serving", "Experiment Tracking", "Engineering Practices", "data governance policies", "AI tools", "graphs", "run".

THE CANDIDATE'S ROLES:
[[rolesJson]]

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES THE JOB POSTING NAMES:
[[postingToolsJson]]

THE SKILLS BLOCK:
[[skillGroupsJson]]

Work only on the entries in THE SKILLS BLOCK above. The examples on this page are not in the block: never list one unless the block itself contains it.

STEP 1 - FIND THE CONCEPTS. Most are written in lower case or as a phrase of ordinary words; a tool has a product name. A product name is a tool even when this candidate's roles never mention it, and every tool the posting names is a tool: leave tools out of this list. Protocols, API standards, query languages, message brokers, code hosts and design applications are tools too - REST, gRPC, GraphQL, Kafka, WebSockets, GitHub, AutoCAD stay in the block. So do named methodologies and named technologies - Agile, Scrum, MLOps, DevOps, CI/CD, LLMs, RAG: a name is not a concept.
For each concept, give the one or two real tools this candidate would have used for that work, fitting their roles, their years and this posting: "regression detection" becomes the test framework of their language, "Experiment Tracking" an experiment-tracking tool, "Model Serving" the serving framework they used. If that tool is already in the block, give [] - the concept simply leaves the block.
Set "bullet" to false ONLY for a bare verb or filler word ("run", "iterate"). Every other concept is true: it will be written into an experience bullet.

STEP 2 - FIX THE TOOLS THAT STAY. Never remove, rename or replace an entry from TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES THE JOB POSTING NAMES: the posting's own spelling is the one a scanner looks for. Fixing its capital letters is the one change allowed.
- "rename": a tool written in the wrong form, with its official name and casing - "C Sharp" becomes "C#", "pytorch" becomes "PyTorch". A library written as its lower-case import name goes here too: "numpy" becomes "NumPy", "scipy" becomes "SciPy", "networkx" becomes "NetworkX", "openapi" becomes "OpenAPI".
- "remove": a tool that is a second form of another entry - a nickname, short name or older name beside the official one ("K8s" beside "Kubernetes", "Postgres" beside "PostgreSQL"). Keep one form of each.

STEP 3 - NAMES WRITTEN IN LOWER CASE. List under "lowercase" every tool in the finished block - kept, renamed, a replacement or an addition - whose makers write the PRODUCT's name starting in lower case: "dbt", "pytest", "pandas", "iOS", "eBPF", "gRPC". Spell each exactly the official way. Judge by the product's name, not the package you import: most libraries are imported in lower case and named with capitals, so numpy, scipy, networkx, boto3 and requests are not on this list (NumPy, SciPy, NetworkX, Boto3, Requests). When unsure, leave a name off: every other tool will have each word capitalised. A name the posting or the candidate's roles write with a capital letter - Terraform, Kubernetes, Docker - is never on this list, and the application ignores this list for any name nobody wrote in lower case.

STEP 4 - ADD TOOLS. With the concepts gone, the block must still hold at least 35 real tools and no more than 45, and every group at least five. Add the real tools this candidate's roles and this posting plainly imply - the ordinary companions of tools already there: a Python service has a web framework and a test framework, a cloud has its storage and monitoring services, a data pipeline has a scheduler and a warehouse. Write each in its official casing, under the block's own heading it belongs to. Never a tool already in the block, never one from an industry they have not worked in, never one that postdates their roles.

RETURN ONLY JSON, no markdown:
{
"concepts": [ { "entry": "the entry exactly as written", "tools": ["Tool"], "bullet": true } ],
"rename": [ { "entry": "the entry exactly as written", "name": "Official Name" } ],
"remove": [ "the entry exactly as written" ],
"additions": [ { "name": "Tool", "group": "Heading" } ],
"lowercase": [ "dbt" ]
}
